name: Abraham
bio:
Abraham (originally Abram) is the father of faith in the Bible. Genesis 12 records that God called him to leave his home in Ur and go to the place God would show him, promising to make him into a great nation, to make his name great, and to bless all the families of the earth through him — a promise later understood to point toward Christ. Though Abraham was childless at the time, and already well past the age for having children, he still believed God's promise of a son, and this faith "was credited to him as righteousness" (Genesis 15:6), making him a model of faith in both Jewish and Christian tradition.

## 👤 Identity and Background: Called Out of His Own Land and Family

Abram was the son of Terah, living in Ur alongside his brothers Nahor and Haran. When Haran died young, Terah set out with Abram, Lot (Haran's son), and his daughter-in-law Sarai, leaving Ur for Canaan — but settled instead in Haran, where Terah died (Genesis 11:27-32). After this, God personally called Abram to continue on into the land of Canaan that He had promised.

## 📖 Core Story: Promise, Testing, and a Journey of Faith

1. **Called and Promised**: God called Abram to leave his country, his people, and his father's household, promising to make him into a great nation, to bless him, to make his name great, and that through him all the families of the earth would be blessed (Genesis 12:1-3).
2. **Faith and Weakness Together**: Wherever Abram went he built altars and called on the name of the LORD, interceded for Sodom, and met Melchizedek, giving him a tenth of everything. Yet he also twice lied out of fear, claiming Sarah was his sister, and — unwilling to wait on God's promise — followed Sarai's plan to father Ishmael through her servant Hagar, planting the seeds of lasting family conflict.
3. **The Test of Offering Isaac**: God asked him to offer up his long-awaited son Isaac as a burnt offering. Abraham obeyed without hesitation, and God provided a ram at the last moment to take Isaac's place, showing that God Himself would provide a substitute sacrifice (Genesis 22).

## ✨ Key Character and Theological Significance

- **A Model of Justification by Faith**: Abraham believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6); Paul uses him in Romans to show that a person is justified by faith, not by works (Romans 4).
- **The Recipient of the Covenant**: God made an everlasting covenant with Abraham, promising descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven and the sand of the seashore, giving the whole land of Canaan to his descendants, and giving circumcision as the sign of this covenant (Genesis 17).
- **The Source of Blessing to the Nations**: His name was changed from Abram ("exalted father") to Abraham ("father of many nations") — he became the ancestor of Israel through Isaac and of many nations through Ishmael, and the New Testament calls him "the father of all who believe" (Romans 4:11).

Abraham's life proves that real faith is not flawless perfection, but choosing again and again to trust God's promises even in weakness and failure, and willingly following His leading.
